environment.description: Same CI/CD runner binary deployed on RHEL 9.2 with SELinux in enforcing mode. The runner process is confined under a custom SELinux type 'cirunner_plugin_t' with a targeted policy module (cirunner-plugin.pp v2.3). The type transition rule 'type_transition cirunner_plugin_t ci_artifact_file_t:file' restricts file creation exclusively to paths labeled 'ci_artifact_file_t' (/var/lib/ci-runner/artifacts/**). The policy includes 'neverallow cirunner_plugin_t ~ci_artifact_file_t:file { write create append }' preventing writes outside the artifact spool. Additionally, the boolean 'cirunner_can_write_cache' is set to 'off', which removes the 'allow cirunner_plugin_t ci_cache_file_t:file { write create }' rule from the active policy. The heap corruption from the double-free still occurs, but the post-exploitation file write to /var/lib/ci-runner/cache/ (labeled ci_cache_file_t) or any path outside artifacts/ is denied by the MAC policy with an AVC denial, preventing the attacker from achieving arbitrary file write.
